text:
aisha: customer reports intermittent TLS handshake failures when their eu-west private deployment calls our us-west region endpoints. started ~0900 UTC after last infra deploy. they see 502/SSL alert and occasional inexplicable 524 timeouts. ticket #7891. attaching short logs and curl output.

mike: do failures correlate with specific AZs or NATs? any pattern on source IPs?

aisha: seems cross-region only. direct calls to hosted api OK. only via their VPC peered route to our private egress. sample curl error: 
`curl -v https://api.internal.redwood --resolve api.internal.redwood:443:3.12.45.67`
response: "SSL connection reset by peer" intermittently.

juan: can you run `dig +short @10.2.3.4 api.internal.redwood` from both eu-west and us-west resolver VMs and paste outputs? suspect DNS divergence.

aisha: eu-west dig ->
`3.12.45.67`
`3.12.45.68`
us-west dig ->
`18.214.33.12`
`18.214.33.13`

mike: aha — different A sets by region. If cert rotation happened and old instances still serve old cert, SNI mismatch would break TLS. traceroute from eu-west shows it hits an old NAT/EGW that routes to 3.12.45.67 which is serving the previous cert.

jane-cse: customer said they rotated certs yesterday. if eu-west still resolves to old IPs, you'll get intermittent handshake failures when traffic hits the stale pool. good catch.

juan: checked infra logs — the private hosted zone replication job errored at 08:45 UTC due to an IAM token refresh failure. That prevented the new ALB A records from propagating to secondary regions. additionally, eu-west resolver instances lost outbound access to our Route53 inbound endpoints because a recent SG tighten blocked outbound to 53/UDP to our central resolver IP, so resolvers fell back to local caches. combination caused stale answers.

mike: can you confirm certs with `openssl s_client -connect 3.12.45.67:443 -servername api.internal.redwood` vs `openssl s_client -connect 18.214.33.12:443 -servername api.internal.redwood`? paste cert CNs.

aisha: ran checks — 3.12.45.67 cert CN=api.internal.redwood (issued 2025-07-01, serial OLD123) vs 18.214.33.12 cert CN=api.internal.redwood (issued 2026-03-10, serial NEW789). so eu-west was hitting old cert.

juan: remediation plan:
1) temporarily lower private hosted zone TTL to 60s (to speed swap)
2) re-run replication job and fix IAM token rotation root cause (will open infra PR)
3) flush caches on eu-west resolver fleet: `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` and restart dnsmasq where applicable
4) patch security group to allow outbound to our route53 inbound/resolver IPs and to us-west A pool on 443/53 as required
5) invalidate ALB target group/stickiness to drain stale instances
6) add alert for DNS divergence in monitoring (cross-region A record mismatch)

ops-bot: change request approved by eng-infra. patch id: CHG-1122. scheduled immediate.

mike: applying SG delta now: allowing outbound 53 UDP/TCP to 10.10.10.5/32 (central resolver) and outbound 443 to 18.214.33.0/24.

aisha: flushed caches on 4 eu-west resolvers and restarted dnsmasq. re-ran dig -> now all regions return 18.214.33.12/13. lowered TTL back to 300 after stabilization.

jane-cse: customer retested via their private route: TLS handshakes stable for 35m, no 502s, latency back to baseline. they asked for a short RCA and a runbook.

juan: root cause summary: hosted-zone replication failure (IAM token issue) + tightened SGs causing resolver fallback to stale caches -> cross-region DNS divergence -> some traffic hit old ALB instances with expired/old certs causing TLS resets.

mike: follow-ups: create infra ticket to fix token refresh and add unit test for hosted-zone replication, add monitoring for A-record mismatch across regions, and deploy a pre-check in deploy pipeline that verifies routing+DNS consistency for private zones. assigning to eng-infra.

aisha: closing thread for now. marking ticket #7891 resolved and will send RCA to customer. :white_check_mark:

juan: also adding a short runbook to /internal/runbooks/dns-cross-region.md with commands used above and rollback steps.

ops-bot: CHG-1122 closed successfully at 1763465400.
